crash.title: Something went wrong
crash.body: Your progress stays on this device. Reload to continue.

game.head: Game
game.highlightWrongFoot: Colours a digit you placed red when it doesn’t match the solution, and has VoiceOver say so. Off by default. Ink mode always shows its blots.
game.autoClearNotesFoot: When you place a digit, it disappears from the notes of the cells in the same row, column and box, and Undo brings them back together with the move. On by default. Ink mode keeps notes by hand. To fill notes with every digit that still fits, press and hold Notes (or press F).
game.highlightPeersFoot: Very lightly tints the row, column and box of the selected cell, so you can see which cells it sees. On by default.

key.head: Recovery key
key.footNone: No account, no email, no password. The key is the only way to bring progress back on another phone — or on this one after its data is cleared.
key.shownOnce: The key is shown this one time only.
key.warn: Keep it somewhere safe. Without the key there is no way to bring progress back, and no way to recover the key itself.
key.deleteKey: Delete key and unlink all devices
key.footCreated: Progress is saved. Enter the key on another phone to continue there.
key.footDanger: A new key replaces the old one only after you confirm you saved it. Deleting the key changes nothing about the puzzles already on this phone.
key.enterHint: Case, spaces and dashes don’t matter. Paste works.
key.footEnter: Whatever is already on this phone is kept and merged with what the key restores.
key.errKey: That key didn’t work. Check it and try again.
key.errLimit: Too many attempts. Try again in {{minutes}} min.
key.errOffline: No connection. Restoring needs the internet — try again once you’re back online.
key.statusFailed: Couldn’t check the recovery key. Check the connection.
key.sheetReMsg: A new key is made and shown once. Your current key keeps working until you check and confirm the new one, so leaving halfway loses nothing. Devices that are already connected stay connected. To disconnect them, use “Unlink this device” or “Delete key and unlink all devices”.
key.sheetUnMsg: It keeps everything already on it and stops syncing with the key.
key.sheetDelTitle: Delete key and unlink all devices?
key.sheetDelMsg: The key is removed from the server and every device stops syncing. Nothing is deleted from the devices themselves.
key.sheetLeaveMsg: It is shown only once. If you leave now, it disappears; a new one can be made with Replace key.
key.shownOnceReplace: The new key is shown this one time only. Your current key keeps working until you check and confirm it.
key.warnReplace: Write it down somewhere safe. Next you’ll enter two of its groups to check it. If the connection drops, just try again — repeating is safe.
key.footReplace: The new key takes over only after you check and confirm it. Until then the current key keeps working on every device.
key.replacedOk: New key is active. The old one no longer works.
key.pendingBody: Your current key still works. The new one was shown once and isn’t active until you confirm it; it can’t be shown again. Valid until {{when}}.
key.errConfirmOffline: No connection, so we can’t tell yet whether the new key is already active. Stay on this screen and try again — repeating is safe.
key.errConfirmGeneric: Couldn’t confirm the new key. Stay on this screen and try again — repeating is safe.
key.errStale: That replacement is no longer valid: it was cancelled, restarted or expired. Your current key still works.
key.sheetReAgainMsg: The key that wasn’t confirmed is discarded, and a new one is made and shown once. Your current key keeps working until you check and confirm the new one. Devices that are already connected stay connected.
key.sheetLeaveReTitle: The new key isn’t confirmed yet
key.sheetLeaveReMsg: It is shown only once. If you leave now, it disappears and your current key keeps working. You can start the replacement again from Settings.
key.verifyIntro: To be sure you wrote the key down correctly, enter two of its groups.
key.verifyHint: Case, spaces and dashes don’t matter. Paste works.
key.verifyMismatch: That doesn’t match. Show the key again, compare the groups and enter them once more.
key.verifySkipNote: You can skip it, but without a written-down key progress can’t be restored on another device.
key.sheetSkipMsg: Without a written-down key your progress can’t be restored on another device, and this key can’t be shown again.
key.sheetSkipReMsg: The new key will take over and the old one will stop working, without a check that you wrote it down. Without a written-down key progress can’t be restored on another device, and this key can’t be shown again.

extras.head: Extras
extras.petFoot: A tiny ink blot on your result card and on a day in Year. It reacts to how the day went and never comes onto the board. Off by default.

grid.title: Grid ∞
grid.p1: Your own grid that never resets. Each daily puzzle you solve on Today adds one clue to it: the cell you filled last. Archive days and Play don’t add clues.
grid.p2: Once the clues are enough for a single answer, it says “{{enough}}”. That usually takes 30 to 60 clues, one a day.
grid.p3: You can’t play it yet. For now it only fills up, one clue per solved day.

fixes.title: Fixes
fixes.p1: How many times you erased a digit, replaced it or took it back with Undo. Pencil notes don’t count.
fixes.p2: A solve with no fixes is “clean”. In ink mode, blots are counted instead.

technique.title: Technique reached
technique.p1: The hardest technique that any digit of your solve needed.
technique.p2: From easiest: Naked Single, a cell that fits only one digit. Hidden Single, a digit that fits only one cell in its row, column or box. Then Locked Candidates and Pairs, which rule digits out by looking at several cells together.

hints.title: Hints
hints.p1: The bulb at the top opens a ladder of four steps: where to look, which technique, which cells, and why. Each step gives a little more. It never says the digit — that part is yours.
hints.p2: The first hint that explains something marks the day “with help”, in the year and on its card; more hints that day change nothing. A day with help doesn’t count as clean in the year’s totals. If Pundoku finds nothing to explain, nothing is marked.
hints.p3: It can name Naked and Hidden Singles, Locked Candidates and Pairs. Ink mode and Grid ∞ have no hints.

year.title: Year marks
year.solved: Finished that day’s puzzle on the day.
year.fixes: Solved, with at least one fix.
year.late: Solved after that day. Your year keeps it as “solved late”, with its own mark.

counter.title: Numbers on the pad
counter.p1: The small number under a digit is how many more of it fit on the grid: nine minus the ones already placed, right or wrong.
counter.p2: “N cells left” counts the empty cells. A wrong digit still fills its cell, so a full grid can be unsolved.

play.preparingLong: Some puzzles take a little longer.
play.fillMessage: Notes go into every empty cell that has none yet, with the digits that still fit. Undo takes it all back in one step.

hint.noteFilled: Notes go in empty cells only
hint.inkFilled: This cell is filled — ink doesn’t lift

hint.nudge: **Stuck?** There’s a hint at the top.

rule.title: A hint marks the day
rule.lead: Pundoku never fills a cell for you. A hint walks you to the next move in four steps: where to look, which technique, which cells, and why.
rule.lead_glyphs: Pundoku never places a shape for you. A hint walks you to the next move in four steps: where to look, which technique, which cells, and why.
rule.r1: The day is recorded as **solved with help** — in the year and on the card.
rule.r2: Further hints today don’t change the mark.
rule.r1Play: The game is marked **with help** on its result card.
rule.r2Play: Further hints in this game don’t change the mark.
rule.r3: If Pundoku finds nothing to explain, nothing is marked.
rule.r4: Ink mode has no hints at all.

s1.body: There’s a move here you can make right now.

s2.naked_single: One cell in there has a single candidate left.
s2.hidden_single: In this region one digit has only one place left to go.
s2.hidden_single_glyphs: In this region one shape has only one place left to go.
s2.locked_pointing: In this box one digit is confined to a single line — so it can leave that line everywhere else.
s2.locked_pointing_glyphs: In this box one shape is confined to a single line — so it can leave that line everywhere else.
s2.locked_claiming: In this line one digit only fits inside a single box — so it can leave the rest of that box.
s2.locked_claiming_glyphs: In this line one shape only fits inside a single box — so it can leave the rest of that box.
s2.naked_pair: Two cells here hold the same two candidates and nothing else — those digits belong to them.
s2.naked_pair_glyphs: Two cells here hold the same two candidates and nothing else — those shapes belong to them.
s2.hidden_pair: Two digits here fit in only two cells — those cells can drop everything else.
s2.hidden_pair_glyphs: Two shapes here fit in only two cells — those cells can drop everything else.

s3.cellBody: That one cell is where the move happens. The digit is still yours to find.
s3.cellBody_glyphs: That one cell is where the move happens. The shape is still yours to find.
s3.pair: Two cells: row {{r1}} column {{c1}}, row {{r2}} column {{c2}}.
s3.pairBody: The pair lives here. Everything it frees is one step further.
s3.lockedBody: Which cells that frees is one step further.

s4.naked_single: Look at the row, column and box of the underlined cell. The circled cells already use eight of the nine digits — the ninth has nowhere else to go.
s4.naked_single_glyphs: Look at the row, column and box of the underlined cell. The circled cells already use eight of the nine shapes — the ninth has nowhere else to go.
s4.naked_single_assumed: Look at the row, column and box of the underlined cell. The circled cells already use up some of the digits, and the candidates you struck in your notes rule out the rest — the one left has nowhere else to go.
s4.naked_single_assumed_glyphs: Look at the row, column and box of the underlined cell. The circled cells already use up some of the shapes, and the candidates you struck in your notes rule out the rest — the one left has nowhere else to go.
s4.hidden_single_one: {{Region}}, one digit is still missing. The circled cell already holds it and rules out every other free square there. Only the underlined cell is left.
s4.hidden_single_glyphs_one: {{Region}}, one shape is still missing. The circled cell already holds it and rules out every other free square there. Only the underlined cell is left.
s4.hidden_single_other: {{Region}}, one digit is still missing. The circled cells already hold it and between them rule out every other free square there. Only the underlined cell is left.
s4.hidden_single_glyphs_other: {{Region}}, one shape is still missing. The circled cells already hold it and between them rule out every other free square there. Only the underlined cell is left.
s4.locked: {{Source}}, one digit only fits in the circled cells, all of them {{target}}. Wherever it lands there, it can’t also sit elsewhere {{target}} — strike it from the underlined cells.
s4.locked_glyphs: {{Source}}, one shape only fits in the circled cells, all of them {{target}}. Wherever it lands there, it can’t also sit elsewhere {{target}} — strike it from the underlined cells.
s4.naked_pair: The two circled cells share the same pair of candidates and nothing else. Between them they will use both digits, so no other cell {{region}} can — strike them from the underlined cells.
s4.naked_pair_glyphs: The two circled cells share the same pair of candidates and nothing else. Between them they will use both shapes, so no other cell {{region}} can — strike them from the underlined cells.
s4.hidden_pair: {{Region}}, two digits fit only in the two circled cells. So those two cells can hold nothing else — strike every other candidate there.
s4.hidden_pair_glyphs: {{Region}}, two shapes fit only in the two circled cells. So those two cells can hold nothing else — strike every other candidate there.
s4.assumes: Part of this relies on candidates you already struck in your notes.

bad.title: Something here doesn’t add up
bad.dup: Two of your digits {{region}} are the same, so the grid can’t be finished as it stands. Pundoku won’t point at the cell — hints come back once it works again.
bad.dup_glyphs: Two of your shapes {{region}} are the same, so the grid can’t be finished as it stands. Pundoku won’t point at the cell — hints come back once it works again.
bad.generic: The grid can’t be finished with what’s {{region}}. Pundoku won’t point at the cell — hints come back once it works again.

none.title: Nothing Pundoku can explain
none.body: This position needs a technique Pundoku doesn’t teach yet — an X-Wing or beyond. Nothing on your board is wrong.
none.foot: Nothing was revealed, so the day stays unmarked.
none.footPlay: Nothing was revealed, so the game stays unmarked.

result.pathSub: Every cell shaded by when you filled it.
result.heatLabel: Heat map of the order in which you filled the grid.

today.gridLabel_one: Your permanent grid: {{count}} clue so far, {{state}}
today.gridLabel_other: Your permanent grid: {{count}} clues so far, {{state}}
today.gridTap: Each daily puzzle you solve adds a clue here.
today.gridExplain: Each daily puzzle you solve adds one clue. It usually takes 30 to 60 before the grid has a single answer.

year.emptyLine: Your year starts today. Each day you play leaves one mark here.

state.lateHelpCorrections: solved late, with help and fixes

card.unfinishedNote: You started this one and left it with {{n}} of {{total}} cells filled in correctly.
card.lateNote: Solved after its day — your year keeps it as “solved late”.
card.lateWarning: If you solve it now, your year keeps it as “solved late”.

ink.foot: Choose before you place your first digit. Notes don’t count.

rule.title: Ink doesn’t lift
rule.lead: In ink mode every digit you place is final. Read this before you start — you can’t switch later.
rule.r1: No undo, and no eraser for digits.
rule.r2: A wrong digit leaves a blot: the cell seals, and the right digit is filled in for you.
rule.r3: Pencil marks still work, and can still be erased.
rule.r4: Once you place a digit you can’t switch back for this puzzle.

ink.blotSay: Wrong digit. The cell is sealed with a blot.
ink.cellBlot: Row {{row}}, column {{col}}, wrong digit. Cell sealed with a blot. {{digit}}

timelapse.none: Replay isn’t available for this day — moves weren’t kept.
timelapse.title: Your solve
timelapse.stepNote: Reduce Motion is on, so the replay opens step by step. Nothing animates.
timelapse.contactNote: Nine stages of your solve. Nothing moves.
timelapse.fpSub: No digits from the solution — safe to post.
timelapse.fpRhythmSub: Tone is the order you filled cells; size is how long you thought.
timelapse.fpFailed: Couldn’t make the image. Try again.

modes.head: Modes
modes.foot: Free games aren’t recorded in your year.
modes.discard: Your unfinished puzzle ({{meta}}) will be discarded.

classic.name: Classic
classic.desc: Plain sudoku: notes, undo and hints are all there.

ink.name: Ink
ink.desc: Every digit is final: no undo and no eraser for digits. A wrong one leaves a blot.

liar.name: Liar
liar.desc: One of the given digits is a lie. Find it, then press and hold it to accuse.

lantern.name: Lantern
lantern.desc: Your digits and notes show only in the row, column and box of the selected cell. Givens stay visible. Touch and hold the board to see it all.
lantern.list: Your digits and notes show only in the row, column and box of the selected cell.

glyphs.name: Glyphs
glyphs.desc: Nine shapes instead of digits. The same logic, without a single number.

melody.name: Melody
melody.desc: Each digit you place sounds a note. A solved grid plays its own tune.

liar.cellCaught: Row {{row}}, column {{col}}, clue {{digit}}; the lie {{lie}} is struck out
liar.menuDesc: The {{digit}} in row {{row}}, column {{col}}. If it’s honest, it’s acquitted — no penalty.
liar.compare_one: Your average catch move: {{avg}} ({{count}} earlier game)
liar.compare_other: Your average catch move: {{avg}} ({{count}} earlier games)
liar.compareFirst: Your first catch — nothing to compare with yet.

melody.hint: Each digit you place plays a note. Mute: the ⋯ menu or the silent switch.
melody.tlNote: Real rhythm, long pauses shortened. The tune follows the replay.

lantern.inspectHint: Or touch and hold the board

status.dark: Tap a cell to light its row, column and box.
status.hold: Inspecting the board — lift your finger to return
